key_insight: A hybrid SCAPS-1D plus machine-learning workflow can rapidly rank multilayer perovskite solar-cell architectures and pinpoint the material descriptors that most strongly drive efficiency.
engineering_relevance: This approach gives device engineers a practical way to narrow a huge ETL/absorber/HTL design space and prioritize high-efficiency, lead-free perovskite stacks before full simulation or fabrication.
method: Trained an ML model on a representative subset to predict PCE for untested structures.
Used SHAP to identify the most influential descriptors and verified top candidates with full device simulations.
evidence_signal: Leave-One-Group-Out cross-validation showed strong ranking performance, and the best verified devices reached 28.85% PCE for FTO/TiO2/Cs2AgBiBr6/NiO/Ag and 28.62% for FTO/SnO2/Cs2AgInBr6/NiO/Ag.
watch_item: The model’s transferability depends on the quality and coverage of the simulated training set, so predictions outside the explored material space may be less reliable.
paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
